 | logout Deering and Turner to Host Mobile DMV and I-Cash Event in Forsyth 
 November 5, 2026 | 0   
 State Representative Regan Deering
 Sen. Sally Turner
     DECATUR, IL… State Representative Regan Deering (R-Decatur) and Senator Sally Turner (R-Beason) are partnering with the Illinois Secretary of State’s office to host a Mobile DMV event on Monday, November 23, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the Forsyth Public Library, located at 268 S. Elwood St. in Forsyth.       The Illinois Treasurer’s office will also be on-site to help residents search for unclaimed property and file claims through the I-Cash program.       “I’m happy to partner with the Secretary of State and Treasurer’s offices to bring these services to residents of the 88th District,” said Rep. Deering. “Our previous Mobile DMV and I-Cash events have been very successful, and I encourage anyone who needs these services to take advantage of this opportunity before the holidays. Thank you to both offices for helping bring these services to our communities.”       “Bringing state services directly into our communities makes it easier and more convenient for residents to take care of important needs without having to travel to a DMV facility,” said Senator Sally Turner. “I’m glad to partner with Representative Deering and the Secretary of State and Treasurer’s offices to offer this opportunity in Forsyth. Whether you need to renew your license, apply for a REAL ID, or check for unclaimed property, I encourage residents to take advantage of these services close to home.”       The following DMV services will be available: Driver’s license renewals and corrections 
 New, renewal, and corrected state ID cards 
 Vehicle sticker sales 
 Organ and tissue donor information and registration 
 Motor voter registration 
 REAL ID applications 
 Driving tests will not be administered. Seniors aged 79 and older must visit a DMV to renew their driver’s license. All payments must be made by personal checks, Visa, MasterCard, American Express, or Discover debit or credit cards. No cash is accepted. 
       Residents with Mobile DMV appointments must bring acceptable identification. Requirements are available at ilsos.gov. The Treasurer’s office will also help residents search for unclaimed property. To conduct a search, residents should provide the last name or business name, the city and ZIP code associated with the Illinois address, and, if available, a first name and property ID.       Additional information may be required to file a claim. Visit icash.illinoistreasurer.com for more information.       Appointments are required for all DMV services, but not for I-Cash assistance. To schedule a DMV appointment, visit RepDeering.com and click the “Mobile DMV Event” button on the homepage, or call Rep. Deering’s office at (217) 876-1968. Posted in Here And There Leave a Comment
